newsitem.title: USA: Kewaunee nuclear plant outage extension seen.
newsitem.headline: Kewaunee nuclear plant outage extension seen.

text.p: A refueling and maintenance outage at Kewaunee Nuclear Power Plant could be extended a few weeks, said plant manager Charlie Schrock.

The plant was shut down September 20 for a 35-day period. However, electronic inspection of some of the tubes in the plant's steam generators has found corrosion that will take more time to fix than expected.
Kewaunee Nuclear is owned by WPS Resources Corp's Public Service Corp, WPL Holdings Inc's Wisconsin Power and Light and Madison Gas & Electric Co.

Total output from the plant was reduced after the last refueling outage, in the spring of 1995, due to corrosion in the small steam generator tubes that transfer heat to the steam system from the reactor system.
Microscopic signs of corrosion found over the last few years are still being analyzed, said Schrock in a statement.
He said it appears a new laser welding technology will be needed to repair the corrosion. Repairs could take an additional three weeks beyond the current schedule.
The work could cost about $3 million to $4 million, said Mark Marchi, nuclear business manager.
